title: A Mobile Manipulator for a Job: Every Check of the Phase Run Against One Job, and the First One That Fails Named

questions.question: What does the capstone report when a job cannot be done?
options: The first requirement that failed, with the figures of all
Every requirement that failed
A yes or a no, and nothing else
The requirement with the worst figure
questions.explanation: The first in the order that fails is the one to deal with first, so it is named. The others are still worked out.

questions.question: A job of 8 kg failed at requirement:
options: 1, parking
3, the payload
6, the travel speed
4, the grasp
questions.explanation: The least of the arm, tipping and traction limits was 4.3 kg, and the job asked for 8.

questions.question: A base that stops to 15 cm failed at:
options: 1, parking
4, the grasp
2, the stopping
None: 15 cm is inside the ring's 35 cm
questions.explanation: The ring's tolerance has to be three times the sigma of the stop. 35 cm is not three times 15.

questions.question: A person 0.45 m from the route failed at:
options: 6, the travel speed
1, parking
None: the person is not on the route
questions.explanation: At 0.45 m the speed a person allows fell below the least speed that is useful, which is the seventh requirement.

questions.question: Is a job that passes proved to work?
options: Yes, for the payload and route that were checked
Yes, when every figure has a margin
Only if the camera is on the hand
No: the checks are simple models with typical numbers, a screen, and the real robot has to be tried
questions.explanation: Passing means nothing known rules it out. The release is a trial on the real robot.

questions.question: Why are the figures of the other requirements kept?
options: So that the report is the same length every time
They are needed to compute the first failure
To be averaged into one score
They show how far each is from passing
questions.explanation: A job that fails at 3 may be close to failing at 6 as well. Seeing all the figures saves fixing one thing and meeting the next.
